chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Joe Keyes, the schoolteacher trumpeter
summary: Keyes played with Bennie Moten and McKinney's, read anything, played melody with the plunger and taught school in Missouri.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What about Joe Keyes? Do you remember Joe Keyes?
Joe Keyes? I knew Joe Keyes when he was playing with Bennie Moten in Kansas City.
Yeah. He was one of the -- he was another underrated trumpet player. Beautiful trumpet player. He could -- I don't care what you put up there, he could read it.

Yeah, and he could play pretty like Joe Smith. He used to play with McKinney's band with the cocked plunger and play melodic things with the cocked plunger, beautiful tone. And he was a well-educated man, too. He was a schoolteacher, too, you know.
Yes, uh-huh. Sure, he taught school out there in Missouri.
